Reaction conditions: HCl/HSCH₂COOH, 60 °C; 6 h. Product: ABDB, consisting of two 4-amino-3-bromophenyl groups attached to a central methine carbon, which is also attached to a 2,4-dichlorophenyl group. ### Synthesis of bis(4-nitro phenyl) chloro phosphonate (MP1) A 1 L, 3-neck, round-bottom flask fitted with a mechanical stirrer, an addition funnel and a condenser with a nitrogen inlet, a thermometer was charged with 4-nitrophenol (102.9 g, 0.74 mol), triethylamine (103 mL, 75 g, 0.74 mol) and tetrahydrofuran (THF, 250 mL). The solution was cooled with an ice water bath. A solution of phosphoryl chloride (POCl₃) (56.8 g, 0.37 mol) in 200 mL of THF was added drop wise over a period of 30 min. The reaction mixture was stirred overnight and allowed to warm to room temperature. The reaction mixture was poured into 1 L of stirred water and the resulting precipitate was collected by vacuum filtration. The solid was dried in a vacuum oven at 55 °C for 4 h to give 110.86 g (85 %) of white crystalline solid¹⁶, m.p. of 118-121 °C. ### Synthesis of bis(4-nitro phenyl) phenyl phosphonate (MP2) This monomer was synthesized by the same way that (MP1) is formed, using materials (dichloro phenyl phosphine oxide) (148.1 g, 0.37 mol) and (4-nitrophenol) (102.9 g, 0.74 mol) where yield 83 %, m.p. = (190-193 °C) and color is light brown **Scheme-III.** **Scheme-III: Synthesis of MP1, MP2** Two related reaction schemes: 1. **MP1 formation:** 4-nitrophenol (O₂N–C₆H₄–OH) reacts with phosphoryl chloride (POCl₃) in Et₃N/THF at 25 °C; 24 h, producing bis(4-nitrophenyl) chloro phosphonate. The phosphorus-containing product has two 4-nitrophenoxy groups and a chlorine substituent on phosphorus. Label: X = Cl = MP1. 2. **MP2 formation:** The corresponding phosphorus reagent is dichloro phenyl phosphine oxide, represented with a phenyl substituent (X = phenyl ring). Reaction with 4-nitrophenol produces bis(4-nitrophenyl) phenyl phosphonate. Label: X = phenyl ring = MP2. POLYENE ANTIBIOTICS. IX AN IMPROVED METHOD FOR THE PREPARATION OF METHYL ESTERS OF POLYENE ANTIBIOTICS RAMESH C. PANDEY, KENNETH L. RINEHART, Jr. Author information * RAMESH C. PANDEY Roger Adams Laboratory, University of Illinois * KENNETH L. Using this method methyl esters of pimaricin, nystatin, eurocidin, hamycin, hamycins A and B, aureofungin, partricins A and B, candimycin, candicidin, and amphotericin B have been prepared and their physical properties are reported. The biological activities of hamycins A and B and their methyl esters are also described.
